_meta.description: Short, general extension-style guidance for the 39 AgroScan classes. It is not a pesticide prescription.
_meta.disclaimer: Always confirm the diagnosis locally and follow the label of any approved product. Mention of a practice does not guarantee effectiveness in every region.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black, velvety spots on leaves; similar scabby lesions can appear on fruit and twigs.
Apple___Apple_scab.management: Remove fallen leaves, prune for airflow and apply a labelled scab fungicide during susceptible periods if the disease is established.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Choose resistant cultivars where available, rake up leaf litter and avoid overhead irrigation.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown leaf spots with purple margins, rotten fruit and rough cankers on branches.
Apple___Black_rot.management: Prune out cankers, remove mummified fruit and apply a labelled fungicide according to local extension guidance.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Keep the canopy open, dispose of infected fruit and maintain tree vigour.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface, often with small rust-coloured pustules underneath.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.management: Protect susceptible trees with a labelled fungicide in spring and remove nearby juniper or cedar hosts where practical.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant resistant apple cultivars and avoid planting highly susceptible apples close to juniper.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Apple___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue routine scouting, especially after rain or humid weather.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain pruning, balanced nutrition and good orchard sanitation.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Blueberry___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Keep monitoring new growth and fruit.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Maintain soil acidity, adequate spacing and good airflow around bushes.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery patches on leaves and shoots; young leaves may curl or distort.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.management: Improve airflow, remove heavily affected shoots and use a labelled powdery-mildew fungicide if spread continues.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen, prune to open the canopy and choose tolerant cultivars.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue monitoring leaves and fruit.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Prune for airflow, manage irrigation and keep orchard litter low.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot_Gray.symptoms: Long, rectangular grey-brown lesions running between the leaf veins, usually starting on lower leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot_Gray.management: Use a labelled fungicide when disease pressure is high and susceptible hybrids are grown; follow local resistance guidance.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot_Gray.prevention: Rotate crops, bury residue and plant resistant hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust.symptoms: Small, reddish-brown powdery pustules scattered on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust.management: Early fungicide may be justified in susceptible fields; late infections often have little yield impact.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids and avoid unnecessary late planting.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green lesions that turn tan and can merge to blight the whole leaf.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.management: Apply a labelled fungicide when lesions appear before tasselling on a susceptible hybrid.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Rotate away from maize, manage residue and use resistant hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue scouting for rust and leaf blights.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops, maintain fertility and choose locally adapted hybrids.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Circular brown leaf spots with dark borders and black dots in the centre; berries shrivel into hard black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.management: Remove mummified fruit, prune out infected wood and follow a labelled fungicide programme from bud break.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Keep the canopy open, remove leaf litter and avoid overhead irrigation.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Interveinal yellowing or browning that gives a tiger-stripe pattern; berries may show dark spotting. The disease affects the woody trunk.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).management: Remove severely affected wood during dry pruning, disinfect tools and avoid vine stress. There is no reliable curative spray.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Use clean planting material, protect pruning wounds and replace severely infected vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular brown to dark-brown lesions on leaves, often with a yellow halo; severe infection causes defoliation.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.management: Improve airflow, remove fallen leaves and apply a labelled fungicide if symptoms are spreading.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Prune for ventilation, avoid excess leaf wetness and keep vineyard litter low.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Grape___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue routine vineyard scouting.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Maintain canopy management, balanced nutrition and good sanitation.

Non_leaf_or_unknown.symptoms: The image is not recognised as a supported close-up leaf, or it does not match any of the 38 known classes.
Non_leaf_or_unknown.management: Retake the photo with a single leaf filling most of the frame, in even light. If the crop is not supported, consult a local expert.
Non_leaf_or_unknown.prevention: AgroScan supports apple, blueberry, cherry, corn, grape, orange, peach, pepper, potato, raspberry, soybean, squash, strawberry and tomato.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetric yellow mottle on leaves, yellow shoots and misshapen, bitter fruit. Symptoms resemble nutrient deficiency.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).management: There is no cure. Manage the Asian citrus psyllid vector, remove confirmed infected trees and use certified nursery stock.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Plant certified disease-free trees, monitor psyllids and report suspected cases to local plant-health authorities.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn purple-brown, often dropping out to create a shot-hole appearance; fruit may develop cracks.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.management: Prune to improve airflow and follow local recommendations for copper or other approved bactericides; avoid excessive nitrogen.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars, avoid overhead irrigation and remove infected twigs.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Peach___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue scouting for bacterial spot and brown rot.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Maintain pruning, orchard sanitation and balanced nutrition.

Pepper___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that become dark and angular, often with yellow halos; heavy infection causes defoliation.
Pepper___Bacterial_spot.management: Remove affected debris, avoid working in wet foliage and use copper-based sprays only where locally approved.
Pepper___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified seed and transplants, rotate crops and avoid overhead irrigation.

Pepper___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Pepper___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue monitoring for bacterial spot and pests.
Pepper___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops, space plants for airflow and water at the base.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown, target-like spots with concentric rings and yellow halos, usually on older lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.management: Apply a labelled fungicide if disease is progressing, remove severely affected leaves and maintain adequate nitrogen.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate away from solanaceous crops, mulch to reduce splash and destroy infected residue.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Irregular, water-soaked grey-green lesions that spread rapidly, often with white fuzzy growth on the underside in humid weather.
Potato___Late_blight.management: Act quickly: remove infected plants, apply a labelled late-blight fungicide and alert neighbouring growers. This disease can destroy a crop within days.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use certified seed, avoid overhead irrigation, destroy cull piles and choose resistant varieties where available.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Potato___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue scouting, especially in cool, wet weather.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Use certified seed, rotate crops and maintain good field sanitation.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Raspberry___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue monitoring canes and fruit.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune old canes, improve airflow and avoid overhead irrigation.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Soybean___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue scouting for foliar diseases and pests.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops, use treated seed where appropriate and maintain balanced fertility.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on the upper leaf surface; leaves may yellow and dry out as the infection spreads.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.management: Improve airflow, remove heavily affected leaves and use a labelled powdery-mildew fungicide or biofungicide.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid crowding and water at the base.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Purple to brown spots scattered on the leaf; edges and tips may look scorched, and heavily infected leaves die.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.management: Remove affected leaves after harvest and apply a labelled fungicide if the disease is spreading.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Use resistant cultivars, improve airflow and avoid overhead irrigation.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Strawberry___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue monitoring leaves and fruit.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Renovate beds, maintain spacing and irrigate at the base.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots with yellow halos; spots may merge and cause leaf drop.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.management: Remove affected debris, avoid handling wet plants and use copper-based sprays only under local recommendations.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified seed, rotate crops and avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings and yellow halos, usually starting on older lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.management: Remove affected leaves, mulch to reduce splash and apply a labelled fungicide if spread continues.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, stake plants for airflow and keep foliage dry.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large greasy grey-green lesions, white fuzzy growth on the underside and rapid collapse of leaves and stems.
Tomato___Late_blight.management: Act immediately: remove and destroy infected plants, apply a labelled late-blight fungicide and warn nearby growers.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation, increase airflow, use resistant varieties and destroy infected residue.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on the upper leaf, with olive-green to grey mold on the underside.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.management: Improve ventilation, reduce humidity, remove affected leaves and use a labelled fungicide if needed.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Control greenhouse humidity, space plants and avoid wetting foliage.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small circular spots with grey centres and dark margins, usually starting on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.management: Remove affected leaves, mulch, avoid splashing water and apply a labelled fungicide if the disease is progressing.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate crops, stake plants and dispose of infected debris.

Tomato___Spider_mites_Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on leaves, bronzing, and delicate webbing on the underside; heavy infestations cause leaf drop.
Tomato___Spider_mites_Two-spotted_spider.management: Spray plants with water to reduce populations, encourage beneficial mites and use a labelled miticide if needed.
Tomato___Spider_mites_Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Keep plants well watered, monitor undersides and avoid excessive dusty conditions.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings, often on leaves and fruit, resembling a target.
Tomato___Target_Spot.management: Remove affected leaves, improve airflow and apply a labelled fungicide if symptoms spread.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Rotate crops, avoid overhead irrigation and manage plant density.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaf margins, stunted growth and reduced fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.management: There is no cure. Remove infected plants and manage whiteflies, which transmit the virus.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties, certified transplants and whitefly monitoring or netting.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic light and dark green mottling, leaf distortion and stunted growth.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.management: There is no cure. Remove infected plants, disinfect tools and hands, and avoid tobacco products near plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties and certified seed; practise strict tool and hand hygiene.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No disease pattern was detected in this image.
Tomato___healthy.management: No treatment is indicated. Continue scouting and maintain good airflow.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops, stake plants, water at the base and monitor for early symptoms.
